sources_considered.why: Read relevant passages on switching and personalization. This official competition analysis discusses both limited consumer switching barriers and possible business-user barriers.
Read the relevant passage in OpenAI's strategy document admitted as a trial exhibit. It records management's claimed advantages and planned moat-building, but does not independently prove durability.
Read the RDX0355 entry to establish the document date and April 23, 2025 public posting.
Read the performance passage. A rival's reported benchmark lead cannot establish the absence of company-wide competitive protection.
The search result incorporates developments after the target period and is not suitable evidence of OpenAI's May 2025 position.

evidence_items.explanation: The authority's analysis gives qualified support to concerns about weak consumer switching barriers, while also discussing possible barriers for business users. It covers the broader market and does not establish that OpenAI lacked every material moat.

evidence_items.publisher: U.S. Department of Justice, publishing an OpenAI trial exhibit
evidence_items.locator: Exhibit RDX0355.005, paragraph immediately before “What is our moat?”
evidence_items.explanation: OpenAI identified brand, research, compute and staffing advantages, but described their persistence conditionally. This earlier management assessment is countervailing context, not proof of a durable May 2025 moat.

unresolved_gaps: No evidence found comprehensively measures the durability of OpenAI's proposed advantages as of May 2025.
The public strategy document is partly redacted and predates the target period.
The competition analysis does not isolate OpenAI's consumer and enterprise switching costs.
The claim supplies no duration or market definition for determining whether an advantage qualifies as a moat.
